decisions.reason: Requiring one email-ready PDF does not change the existing 34-page maximum.
The emailed final PDF can coexist with delivery of editable Canva access and does not revoke ownership or editing rights.
Building the current design for clean PDF export does not resume or alter the deferred reusable modular-template requirement.
The email-ready PDF decision adds an output constraint but does not change the required complete-document layout or its single-pass scope.
The final PDF format and email submission method do not change the requirement to apply supplied tables to the final draft.
The same message separately establishes the fixed section order, which is already represented by a complete candidate Event; the email-ready PDF decision adds no further section-order change.
Submitting one email-ready PDF does not change the required inclusion of the organization chart in the final draft.
The output and submission constraint does not change the requirement to apply photos to the final draft.
The final PDF decision does not alter which final-draft content must be included in the document.
Email-compatible PDF export does not change the Blue Mesa Strategies identity, logo, or color requirements.
This candidate concerns the separate RCP proposal, while the source decision applies to the Civic Canopy RFQ.
The Civic Canopy RFQ email-submission decision does not modify the separate RCP proposal's format-compliance rules.
